assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology to incretin therapy is a clear chain from basic gut-hormone biology to transformative treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with broad and still-growing clinical and physiological impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology, GLP-1 secretion and action), Drucker (GLP-1 receptor biology, intestinotrophic GLP-2) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide) are the most defensible trio; Knudsen's industrial drug-development role and other contributors (e.g. Habener, Habener-lab work) are not in the credited list and the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Extensive independent confirmation in large outcome trials; effects on obesity, cardiovascular and renal outcomes are well established. Timing is strong given the recent clinical dominance.
uncertainties: Credit dispute around who first identified the active GLP-1 peptide versus physiology and drug development
Whether the prize should reward basic discovery or the pharmaceutical translation; my recollection of the precise priority claims is not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that its blockade treats rheumatoid arthritis changed the care of autoimmune and inflammatory disease worldwide and validated cytokine targeting in humans.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini made the decisive translational link from the TNF-dependent cytokine cascade in synovial cultures to clinical anti-TNF trials; the pairing is long recognised (Lasker 2003) and cleanly bounded.
assessment.maturity: Decades of clinical use, multiple agents and indications and independent replication make this fully mature; recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Contributions of others in TNF biology (e.g. Cerami, Beutler, Old) and antibody engineering may be argued as part of the chain
Focus is clinical-translational rather than discovery of a new biological mechanism

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a general method to control genetically defined cells with light, transforming causal circuit analysis across systems and creating a major new methodology with very wide uptake.
assessment.attribution: The channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its adaptation to neurons and circuit work (Deisseroth, Boyden) are both decisive; with a three-person limit I credit Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, which leaves out Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenboeck and is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Very strong independent adoption over more than a decade; the method is mature, though clinical translation is still early.
uncertainties: Competing claims among six credited names with only three slots
Method rather than disease mechanism; Nobel committee precedent for tools exists but the framing is a judgement call

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed to trigger interferon responses, linking innate immunity, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies and lupus), infection and cancer immunity, with a clear and original mechanism including the second messenger cGAMP.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP, and Barber identified STING; this is a compact and defensible pairing. Sun, Wu and Ishikawa made contributions in the same labs and are credited but I consider them trainees or co-discoverers of lesser decisive weight.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and broadly adopted, with a large follow-on literature; therapeutic translation is still in progress, so recognition is somewhat early but the mechanism is stable.
uncertainties: Relative weight of Chen versus Barber and the role of other groups on STING (Ishikawa, Tanaka, Chen) is partly disputed
Clinical benefit of STING modulators is not yet established

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened the field of cell therapy for cancer; this is a major clinical breakthrough built on original conceptual and engineering work.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CAR design with costimulation and clinical translation), June (clinical trials and costimulatory CAR-T success in leukemia) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell therapy) form a plausible trio; Eshhar, Kuwana and others who pioneered chimeric receptors are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and long follow-up exist; independent confirmation is strong in haematological cancer, while efficacy in solid tumours and toxicity remain limits.
uncertainties: Priority of the original chimeric receptor concept is outside the supplied credit
Limited success in solid tumours may temper the timing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cloning of the T-cell receptor solved a central problem of adaptive immunology, the molecular basis of antigen specificity of T cells, and underpins later work on MHC restriction, tolerance and immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: Davis and Hedrick and, independently, Mak and Yanagi cloned the TCR genes in 1984; the credit is a long-standing and genuinely competitive question. I would favour Davis, Hedrick and Mak, which leaves out Yanagi.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of confirmation; its fundamental importance is beyond doubt, although recognition is late.
uncertainties: Fair allocation between the two simultaneous groups remains unresolved
Earlier immunology prizes already honoured adjacent topics such as MHC restriction

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like particle vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, a concrete public-health success derived from a clear and original technical insight.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs; Frazer (with Zhou) developed VLP expression and the vaccine concept in parallel. Zhou Jian, deceased, and industry contributors are not credited; I would choose these three, though there is a priority question.
assessment.maturity: Population-level data show strong reductions in infection and precancer; invasive-cancer reduction data are now emerging, so timing is good. A related prize (zur Hausen, 2008) covers the causal link, which may weigh against.
uncertainties: Priority and credit between the NIH and Queensland groups
Overlap with the 2008 HPV prize for the virus-cancer link

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition provided the proof of principle of targeted, mechanism-based cancer therapy, turning chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal into a chronic disease.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (compound and programme at Ciba-Geigy) and Sawyers (resistance mechanism and next-generation inhibitors) form a plausible trio; the foundational Abl and Philadelphia chromosome findings by others (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) are outside this credit.
assessment.maturity: Decades of outcome data and many replications make this fully mature; the Lasker Award in 2009 was already given for this work.
uncertainties: The discovery component is partly earlier work by others
Drug-development prizes are a debated fit for the Nobel framework
